title: GUI & reactive — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: A young but genuinely coherent GUI plane, built on vendored RmlUi and actually running — windows open, events flow, it renders through the GPU plane and an SVG tier. Two standouts reflect the library's DNA: RTL/bidi fully owned (RmlUi does none — the emitter reverses layout, the engine reorders and shapes via SheenBidi + HarfBuzz), and accessibility built in from the grammar up (a mandatory RATIONALE on every element seeds an ARIA tree exposed to the OS via AccessKit). The rest is early: a closed four-primitive authoring vocabulary, flexbox-only layout, imperative view-binding — and a full reactive runtime that ships but is not yet wired to the GUI. No IME, no theme system, no animation. And the whole plane is on local `main` only, not yet pushed.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: Every lane names what actually ships, the tools it is fair to measure against, and the one thing still owed. Measured against decades-old, enormous frameworks, a young plane shows two distinctive strengths and a wide band of working-but-early basics.

lanes.engine: Fully owned, because RmlUi does no bidi at all. The emitter (`stzUiDocument`) reverses flex rows under RTL, resolves logical `start`/`end` to physical sides, and builds a direction map with inheritance; the engine shaper (`gpu_text.zig`) reorders with SheenBidi (UAX#9) and shapes Arabic with HarfBuzz, feeding RmlUi the widths it will actually paint.
lanes.owed: The peers have built-in bidi; here it is explicit, owned end-to-end, and guarded (including a picture-found bug the asserts had missed). Consistent with the library's first-class Arabic typography — a genuine strength.

lanes.engine: Both halves ship. G4a: every element carries a mandatory RATIONALE that, with ROLE/LABEL, emits an ARIA-role tree (`stzAccessibilityTree`). G4b: `a11y.zig` hands that tree to AccessKit, bridging to UI Automation / NSAccessibility / AT-SPI.
lanes.owed: Accessibility is mandatory at authoring time, not an afterthought — arguably ahead of peers where a11y is opt-in. The sharp edge (adapter must exist before the window shows) is handled and documented.

lanes.engine: A closed four-kind grammar — PANEL / BOX / TEXT / STYLE — with closed field sets, a diagnostics court (unknown field = error), a `.panel`→RML→`.panel` round-trip fixpoint, and mandatory RATIONALE. Emits RML/RCSS (and HTML/CSS for a web projection).
lanes.owed: A coherent, governed authoring layer — but a four-primitive vocabulary is far narrower than the component models of the peers. Breadth is the widget lane (below).

lanes.engine: RmlUi flexbox via RCSS: direction, wrap, gap, padding/margin, align, justify, and px / % / `fill` sizing — emitted as `display:flex` by `stzUiDocument.ring::ToRml()`.
lanes.owed: CSS Grid is refused by decision, and there is no constraint or custom layout. Flexbox covers most UI, but grid-shaped layouts must be composed by hand.

lanes.engine: RmlUi's render interface is a recorder, not a painter (`stz_rmlui.cpp`): it records one flat vertex/index display list, which the graphics plane draws via the GPU tier or an SVG tier — one list, two renderers. GUI output is data crossing a C ABI.
lanes.owed: A clean recorder→GPU/SVG model (the deviceless SVG tier is distinctive) — but it rides the GPU plane's own young f32 renderer, and PNG needs a GPU device.

lanes.engine: A complete input surface in the C ABI: pointer move/button/leave, key, text-input, focus + directional focus move, hit-testing (`element_at`), and an event recorder that counts dropped events. Ring-side focus order and arrow navigation in `stzPanel`.
lanes.owed: The primitives are all there and honest about drops — but no gesture recognition (drag/pinch/swipe) or higher-level event abstractions above raw pointer/key.

lanes.engine: A real reactive stack (`base/reactive`): `stzReactiveObject` with Watch / Computed(deps) / BindTo / SetAttribute (old≠new gating), plus streams, timers, tasks, HTTP and an event bus — running on a libuv reactor (`reactor.zig`) with a no-DLL cooperative fallback.
lanes.owed: A genuine signals runtime with computed dependencies — used by `stzApp` — but its power is not yet reaching the view: see the binding lane, where the two are still unconnected.

lanes.engine: Native windows via vendored GLFW (`window.zig` — HWND / X11 / NSWindow handle, poll→input→draw→present loop with delta time). `stzApp` is a declarative "living world" (graph + workflow + Reaxis + goals + persistence).
lanes.owed: Windows open and a real app model exists — but window management is basic: no multi-window orchestration, dialogs, menus or system-tray, and `stzApp` is more a domain/world model than a conventional window framework.

lanes.engine: RmlUi's own element library supplies the form controls — input, select, textarea, progress, tabset, form, button — over the `.panel` primitives.
lanes.owed: No rich widget set: no tables, trees, menus, dialogs, date/color pickers, toolbars, docking. Basic form controls exist; the library of higher-level widgets the peers are famous for does not.

lanes.engine: The shipped G5 first clause: `{placeholder}` templates and `Set` / `SetStyle` / `Apply` that mutate a live document preserving focus (no rebuild), with values escaped as data so a model can't inject markup.
lanes.owed: Explicitly imperative, not reactive — no dependency graph, no computed, no two-way binding. The whole model React and Flutter are built on (signal → auto-updated view) is the unbuilt G5 second clause (Tier A).

lanes.engine: Single-line text input works (`stz_gui_text_input`); the `ActivateKeyboard` seam is recorded for the future.
lanes.owed: No IME — composition input for CJK and complex scripts is deferred (costed at 1–3 engineer-years), and two-way text editing is undone. Ironic against the strong RTL rendering: the plane can display Arabic beautifully but can't yet compose-type it.

lanes.engine: Inline styling ships — `BACKGROUND`, `COLOR`, reusable `STYLE` bags → RCSS — and a profile layer maps logical spellings to native vs web.
lanes.owed: No semantic theme system (G6 "sense sheet" not started, blocked on an external repo) and no animation / transitions (RmlUi supports them; Softanza doesn't emit them). Both are core to a modern UI.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The first two turn a working foundation into a usable framework — connecting the reactive runtime and filling the widget set; the third is the harder, longer reach.

tiers.title: Tier A — turn foundation into framework

items.title: Wire the reactive runtime to the GUI (G5 clause 2)
items.text: Connect `stzReactiveObject` signals/computed to the imperative view-binding so a state change auto-updates the view — the React/Flutter model. Both halves already ship (a real signals runtime and focus-preserving view mutation); they are simply unconnected. The highest-leverage single move.

items.title: A richer widget set
items.text: Tables, trees, menus, dialogs, toolbars and pickers over the RmlUi element library — the higher-level components the peers are built on. Without them, real apps hand-assemble everything from four primitives.

items.title: The semantic theme system (G6)
items.text: One "sense sheet" artifact → RCSS + CSS variables, so light/dark and brand theming come from a single governed source rather than inline hex. Currently blocked on an external `stzSense` repo — unblock or inline it.

items.title: Animation & transitions
items.text: Emit RCSS transitions/keyframes (RmlUi supports them; the emitter doesn't yet). State changes and focus moves gain motion — the difference between a static form and a live interface.

items.title: Two-way binding & form validation
items.text: Bind an input back to a model with validation and formatting — today binding is one-way and unformatted. It completes the forms story the RmlUi controls already start.

tiers.title: Tier C — the harder, longer reach

items.title: IME & two-way text editing
items.text: Composition input for CJK and complex scripts — the expensive, deferred gap (1–3 engineer-years), and the one that most limits the plane's i18n claim given how well it already renders those scripts.

items.title: Push & cross-platform verification
items.text: The whole plane sits on local main only — not on origin or codeberg — and is built/tested on Windows (GLFW can't cross-compile from Windows; a11y/wgpu/RmlUi are prebuilt Windows DLLs). Push it, and run it on real Linux/macOS hardware to make "cross-platform by design" true in fact.

items.title: Window-framework depth
items.text: Multi-window orchestration, native dialogs, menus and system-tray over the GLFW base — the desktop-app plumbing between "a window opens" and "an application ships."

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: Re-surveyed from `main` (the working branch was stale). The plane genuinely runs and is heavily guarded — 415 GUI assertions across 11 suites (panel, RTL, font, input, accessibility, scene, binding…) plus the reactive suite, all green, with PNG/SVG witnesses (windows open, events flow, Arabic renders). Two delivery facts matter for planning: the entire plane is on local main only, unpushed to origin/codeberg, and it is built and tested on Windows — cross-platform is by design (GLFW / AccessKit / wgpu) but not hardware-verified. The "tick loop" is `RunLoop()` / `Run()` (no literal `Cycle()`), libuv on the engine thread, callbacks on the Ring thread.

Softanza's GUI is an early, coherent, governed plane that already does two things better than most — owned RTL/bidi and grammar-level accessibility — over a real running RmlUi+GPU stack; its distance from Qt/Flutter/React is breadth (widgets), the unbuilt bridge from its own reactive runtime to the view, and the modern-UI table stakes (theming, animation, IME) it has scoped but not yet built.

Ratings reflect what the guards prove.
